note: Explicit AI Blocks source reviews. Exact quotes and hashes support review; they do not automatically prove meaning or establish a human approval or a successful run. Older unreviewed coverage is reported separately.

evidence.quote: The user has passed (or will pass) a markdown file of raw material.
evidence.rationale: The method reads the person’s own raw material file. It does not require an outside article as source_text.

evidence.quote: **Curriculum framework:** Specific standards
evidence.rationale: The optional curriculum framework can arrive as a standards document. The teacher may instead give those facts in the request.

evidence.quote: **Desired outcomes:** What students should understand, know, and be able to do.
evidence.rationale: The request must give learning outcomes, student level and duration. These facts form the required planning question.

evidence.quote: **Teacher observations:** What the teacher has noticed.
evidence.rationale: Written observation notes can supply this evidence. A separate document is optional because the teacher can put the observations in the request.

evidence.quote: **Children's interest:** What has captured their attention.
evidence.rationale: The teacher’s account of the interest and observations supplies the required planning problem. No finished third-party article is required.

evidence.quote: **Discussion purpose:** What the discussion should achieve.
evidence.rationale: Discussion purpose, topic and student level are the required request facts. The method does not ask for an external source article.

evidence.quote: **Emotional context:** The situation prompting this.
evidence.rationale: The teacher provides the classroom context and student level as a planning request. This is not a clinical assessment input.

evidence.quote: **Curriculum links:** Specific objectives to address
evidence.rationale: Curriculum objectives can come from an optional standards document. The method also supplies a fallback when no curriculum links are given.

evidence.quote: **Phenomenon:** The real-world situation.
evidence.rationale: The phenomenon and subjects define the required unit-planning request. Other facts may be supplied in the same request.

evidence.quote: Tell the agent what kind of note to take, and provide the content.
evidence.rationale: The method creates, updates and reads the person’s own notes. document covers that supplied note content without mislabelling it as somebody else’s article.

evidence.quote: Auditing a completed or interrupted agent run from traces and artifacts.
evidence.rationale: Trace events and recorded artifacts supply the evidence being audited. Missing records remain gaps rather than invented successful events.

evidence.quote: immutable code, configuration, model, prompt, tool-schema, and artifact revisions when available;
evidence.rationale: Available configuration and artifact documents can support the audit. They are optional separate files and do not replace required trace evidence.

evidence.quote: declared goal and terminal success criteria;
evidence.rationale: The audit needs the original goal and success contract. It must not invent a stronger or weaker contract.

evidence.quote: **Data class is allowed**: `synthetic`, `deidentified`, or `aggregate`.
evidence.rationale: Only the allowed verified source-fact data can populate a draft. The record does not approve patient-data handling or clinical decisions.

evidence.quote: Study-design-specific reporting guideline and source protocol/SAP
evidence.rationale: A protocol or analysis-plan document can supply optional route-specific source material. Its presence does not establish clinical or regulatory compliance.

evidence.quote: **Purpose is explicit**: publication draft, diagnostic-report scaffold, trial-results manuscript, protocol reporting review, CSR draft, aggregate safety table, or aggregate research summary.
evidence.rationale: The requested reporting purpose selects the route. The existing authority, provenance, local handling and qualified-review gates still apply.

evidence.quote: screening results (sanctions / PEP / adverse media) from whichever screening source the user has.
evidence.rationale: Existing screening findings can arrive as an optional report. They are source evidence, not a fabricated screening result or automatic acceptance.

evidence.quote: Inputs: the structured record from `kyc-doc-parse` (the Onboarding document reader)
evidence.rationale: The checker consumes the extracted structured applicant record. Raw identity images are not the declared input to this step.

evidence.quote: the firm's rules grid (a file the user provides)
evidence.rationale: The firm’s supplied rules grid is required. The method applies that trusted grid to the applicant record without inventing rules.

evidence.quote: Read [the shared voice profile](../../shared/voice-profile.md) before writing anything in the owner
evidence.rationale: An available voice-profile document can guide drafts. The method has an un-voiced fallback when no profile or samples are supplied.

evidence.quote: In pasted mode, ask one extra question up front: what did you promise anyone in the last two weeks?
evidence.rationale: The owner can supply missing commitment context as an answer. That extra input is conditional on pasted mode, so it stays optional.

evidence.quote: The owner forwards a batch or pastes a thread and gets the same triage, the same drafts, the same action items.
evidence.rationale: Pasted or forwarded email is short_text. It is optional because an authorized connected mailbox can supply the messages instead.

evidence.quote: Read from Gmail or Microsoft 365, whichever is connected
evidence.rationale: The connected-mailbox route uses the owner’s authorized account. Connection is optional because the method also accepts pasted messages.

evidence.quote: a list of text chunks with optional metadata and scores
evidence.rationale: Structured retrieval scores and metadata are optional supporting data. Plain text chunks remain a valid input without them.

evidence.quote: Provide the raw context (a list of text chunks with optional metadata and scores)
evidence.rationale: The source bundle consists of supplied text chunks. document names that material without treating every chunk as an outside article.

evidence.quote: the user query, and the target token budget.
evidence.rationale: The actual query and token budget are required to choose and order context. The method does not invent either one.

evidence.quote: The task is whatever follows `/be-ambitious`. If nothing follows, use the user's most recent request.
evidence.rationale: The method starts from the task or prompt the person typed, in their own words, which is a brief. Data, tools and access are optional and listed as present or missing.

evidence.quote: Extract the complete design language from any website URL.
evidence.rationale: The method runs designlang on the website URL the person gives it, so a live web page address is the one required input.

evidence.rationale: The method requires the buyer brief to define the buyer and proposition.

evidence.quote: **The job** (required): what you want done, in your own words.
evidence.rationale: The required question is the person’s own job and desired result; existing work and limits refine the goal rather than changing its required input type.

evidence.quote: **Website address** (required). Pasted pages count, if the site can't be read.
evidence.rationale: The required website source can be a readable URL or pasted pages; an unavailable site remains a named gap rather than an invented business record.

evidence.quote: **Results** (optional): ads, emails, pages or offers that worked or didn't.
evidence.rationale: Optional campaign or store performance exports supply dated results, distinct from claims and from content seen running.

evidence.quote: **Brand material you already have** (optional): product sheets, packaging photos, a style guide, past ads, pasted pages.
evidence.rationale: Optional product sheets and labelled brand materials supply product/offer/asset facts and their provenance for the reusable brain.

evidence.quote: Write one buyer, one reason to buy, one offer.
evidence.rationale: An optional buyer persona narrows the one buyer and buying situation pinned in step 1. The writer can infer a buyer from supplied facts when none is supplied, and must label that inference.

evidence.quote: A ready doubt list from the Unanswered customer question finder works too.
evidence.rationale: The optional objection_map is the prepared buyer-doubt list with evidence/answers. It feeds the same doubt-and-section mapping as raw customer records rather than requiring a second research format.

evidence.quote: Read the existing page before rewriting, retain correct brand language and working buyer choices, and explain changes through the buyer question they resolve.
evidence.rationale: An optional existing page or campaign draft can be the copy_draft being rewritten. It provides current wording to retain or change; the writing result remains copy and a brief, not a built page.

evidence.quote: **Brand look** (required): colours with their jobs, fonts, voice, logo, product photos.
evidence.rationale: The required brand_brain supplies actual visual assets, type, colour, voice and claim boundaries. The method explicitly preserves supplied fonts and colours and separately inspects the existing site and source.

evidence.quote: **The page's case** (required): the copy or brief, the buyer, the ad's promise, the offer, the facts.
evidence.rationale: The required landing_page carries the accepted copy or page brief and its buyer case. Existing-page review also needs actual screenshots/source; a design plan is not an implemented page.

evidence.quote: **Customer words** (optional): supplied reviews, questions or interview excerpts with source IDs.
evidence.rationale: The optional voc_reviews now has an explicit real-method instruction to use sourced customer words when selecting buyer questions and relevant proof. It stays optional, and inferred doubts remain separate from quoted evidence.

evidence.quote: Read the original request, constraints, approved page copy and layout.
evidence.rationale: The required landing_page supplies accepted copy and page content to implement. It is not the source of a verified submission endpoint, current website access or browser-check results.

evidence.quote: The original brief, the approved page copy and the approved layout.
evidence.rationale: An optional separate page_layout_spec supplies the approved section layout; the same layout can already be embedded in the approved copy or original brief. Optionality applies to a separate document, not permission to disregard the accepted layout.

evidence.quote: Resolve the copy and the form destination from the original request and existing approved inputs.
evidence.rationale: A separate brief is optional because the original user request can carry constraints, integration target and buyer action. An unresolved required endpoint or main action blocks launchable status rather than being invented.

evidence.quote: Read the user's original request, brand brain and actual repository before choosing a design or framework.
evidence.rationale: The required question is the actual page-building request, including product and audience facts gathered by the workflow. The broad port does not claim that a question alone supplies repository access, approved assets, verified offers or executed checks.

evidence.quote: **A flat-lay phone photo of the garment** (required). Front only, laid flat on a plain background, nothing folded.
evidence.rationale: The workflow starts from an actual real-garment flat-lay photo; the person later returns actual generated/edited files at explicit checkpoints. The required photo input does not itself supply a marketplace name, image tool, missing garment details or permission to upload/spend.

evidence.rationale: The required product_photos input is the actual garment photograph used as image 1, preserving true colour, fabric and fit. The complete method separately requires an authorised pose/scene reference as image 2, real tool access and cost approval; a garment photo or audit report alone is not sufficient to run it.
